opportunity_thesis: The unit-economics method is sound, but the per-tenant Heavy table counts an operator seat at N=1 and not at N=10/50: either the fail-closed N=1 floor is $300 too high or the N=10 floor is $30 too low (INFERRED from source arithmetic). Token bands are SPECULATIVE. The Heavy seat 'does not include API' while token costs are API-priced, so its tenant role is unclear.

findings.summary: Per-tenant Heavy N=1 floors ($636/$694/$886) include an operator seat; N=10/50 rows do not. Without it N=1 is $336/$394/$586; with it N=10 is $339/$397/$589.
Fail-closed N=1 pricing uses the operator-seat row, so SKU 2 at $800 sits under the $886 high floor; without the operator seat it clears $586.
The Heavy seat 'does not include API', yet tenant token costs are priced at API rates; the seat's tenant role is unstated.
'high+cliff x2 = $512' is listed but used in no floor row.
